label: GPT-6.1 Terra
output:
I’ve been thinking about Kavya’s post since yesterday. A lot of people in our Foundry91 cohort know it’s about DabbaDost, and some have tagged me. I don’t want this to become a public fight, but I do want to own what I got wrong and clear up a few things.

Kavya and I were both in cohort 4. Before our demo day in March 2026, she sat with me in the Koramangala office until 1 am helping fix our Razorpay webhook mess. I haven’t forgotten that. She’s a friend, someone I respect, and someone who has helped us when she didn’t have to.

Here’s what happened from our side.

We posted a backend developer opening on our LinkedIn page and Instahyre on 14 September. It was open to anyone. One person applied on 19 September; the other came through their referral two weeks later. Nobody from our side DMed either of them. Both joined us on 3 November.

The offers were 22% over their then-current CTC, not 40%. I’m putting the number here because 40% is already being repeated, and I don’t want an incorrect figure to become the story.

There was also a claim that we promised ESOPs we don’t have. DabbaDost does have an ESOP pool. It’s small, but it’s real and has been on paper since January.

That said, there’s a part I handled badly. I knew from day one that both people worked at SitterNest. I should have called Kavya before making the offers, not after. I WhatsApped her after the second offer was accepted, but by then I’d missed the moment to have that conversation properly. That’s on me, and I’m sorry, Kavya.

I also want to be clear that the people who joined us made their own decisions. They didn’t ask to be part of a public conversation, so I’m leaving their names out.

We’re a batch of 11 startups hiring from a small pool, often in the same HSR and Koramangala circles. This kind of situation will come up again. Could we agree on a simple cohort rule: if you’re interviewing someone from another batch company, give that founder a heads-up before making an offer?

Kavya, I respect you and what you’re building at SitterNest. I hope we can talk about this directly. Coffee or a call this week, whenever you’re comfortable. @Kavya
